summary: TechCrunch interviews Twitch Chief Monetization Officer Mike Minton after a tense year of creator backlash over the ended 70/30 subscription split and the restrictive Partner Plus launch. Twitch shifted Partner Plus to a points-based system, walked back its embedded ad restrictions, and announced new ad controls and simulcasting at TwitchCon 2023. Minton says the 350-sub threshold is arbitrary and could come down, and describes ads, subscriptions and Amazon-powered sponsorships as Twitch's three monetization pillars.
one_line: Twitch's Mike Minton explains Partner Plus changes, ad improvements and sponsorship plans as Twitch tries to rebuild trust with streamers after monetization backlash.
key_facts: Twitch announced last year it would end the 70/30 subscription revenue split deal offered to select streamers in favor of prioritizing ad revenue.
In June 2023, Twitch launched Partner Plus, giving eligible creators a 70/30 subscription revenue split on the first $100,000 they make per year.
Partner Plus originally required at least 350 monthly paid subscriptions, and gift subs and monthly subs via Amazon Prime did not count.
On August 28, 2023, Twitch changed Partner Plus eligibility to points: Tier 1, 2 and 3 subs earn 1, 2 and 6 points respectively.
Twitch walked back its policy restricting embedded ads and other sponsored content after backlash from streamers who rely on branded content.
Dan Clancy became Twitch CEO earlier in 2023 and has prioritized engaging with streamers; community sentiment at TwitchCon in Las Vegas was significantly more positive than the prior year.
At the TwitchCon keynote, Twitch announced more streamer control over ad breaks and allowing simulcasting to other livestreaming platforms.
Mike Minton said the 350 criterion is arbitrary and could easily come down, and that Partner Plus is 'the beginning,' not the end.
To win streamers over to ads, Twitch increased the ad rev share and launched the ad incentive program; new features let moderators know when an ad break is coming and adjust it around content.
Minton named three monetization pillars: viewer support (subscriptions, gifting, cheering), advertising, and sponsorships, where he says Twitch is behind.

Minton said Twitch is part of Amazon, which he called the third largest and fastest growing advertising business in the world, and aims to let Amazon advertisers set up influencer deals programmatically.
Minton said the Partner Plus launch, simulcasting and the embed changes were driven by community feedback, not competitive pressure from platforms like YouTube or Kick.
